# OpenProgram 1.3.0 Release Notes

OpenProgram 1.3.0 shows every connected provider's health, quota and spend on one page, lists the agents working in a conversation with their status and cost, and opens the files an agent makes without the model having to attach them. Which packages this release carries is stated below; anything that could not be built is listed under "Not in this release".

## ✨ New features

- **Providers page.** Each connected provider shows its health, its quota and its spend over the last 30 days, as cards or as rows. Adding a provider takes three steps, starts from the common ones, and offers a key that is already in your environment.
- **The model picker says what is wrong.** A model that is not set up, or whose quota is nearly used, is marked in the picker. A spent quota offers another model instead of a raw error, a provider out of credit says "No credit" with a Top up link instead of asking you to sign in again, and a subscription shows "Included" rather than a dollar price.
- **A roster of agents in Activity.** The Activity panel lists the conversation's agent with the helpers it started under it, each with a status (Running, Needs approval, Needs input, Stalled, Waiting, Failed, Idle) and what it has cost. Finished helpers fold into one "N finished" row, the header adds up what the helpers cost, and Stop all stops every one that is still going.
- **Sub-agents on one line.** An agent that runs in another conversation is one row in the reply: its name, state, task, time and cost. Opening it shows its final reply and the files it changed, with Switch and Cancel.
- **Compact messages between agents.** A message from one agent to another, and the reply to it, are one-line rows named after the sender that open in place to the full text; they no longer look like messages you typed.
- **Approvals name who is asking.** When a sub-agent needs your approval, the card in your conversation carries its name; so do the terminal prompt and a channel message. Your answer lets that agent go on.
- **Delegation settings on the Agents page.** "Other agents can use it" decides whether an Agent is offered to other agents, and "When delegated" decides where it works when another agent starts it: Automatic, Same folder or Own worktree.
- **Files an agent makes open on their own.** A deliverable a turn produced gets a file card without the model attaching it, file paths in a reply are links that open the preview, and paths, file cards and changed-file rows share one right-click menu. Sending a file to its own chat is no longer held for review.
- **A Goal keeps going after a failure.** A Goal whose turn failed continues by itself, up to three failures in a row, instead of waiting paused for Continue. A turn you stopped and a spent budget still wait for you.
- **The Office editor can be installed.** This release carries the Office editor's files, and the App downloads them from its own version's release.

## 🐞 Bug fixes

- **Goals.** A reply in a conversation with a Goal no longer turns into "GoalConflictError", and a Goal follows only its own branch, so a reply on another branch does not block it. A Goal left active after its turn ended becomes a pause you can resume. `/goal status` shows the status instead of saving a goal named "status", and `/goal` typed in a new chat stays in that chat.
- **Files.** A model asked to send a file no longer answers that `send_file` is unavailable, and a reply says a file was not sent only when it was refused. A file card comes only from a file the turn really made: links and marker text in a reply no longer create cards or open the preview, and a script the agent wrote to build a deliverable gets no card of its own. A chat with no project can open and send the files it made in its working folder.
- **Context ring.** The ring divides by the model's real window instead of a made-up 128k limit, shows only the count when the model is unknown, reads the same number as its popover, and keeps its estimate through the first Send of a new chat.
- **Stopping and rewinding.** A stopped reply is the same text in the stream, after a reload, in `--print` and in channels, and neither Stop nor a steer keeps text that never reached the screen. A Stop reaches a running tool at once on the async turn API. A Rewind sent twice gets the first answer instead of a refusal.
- **Sending.** A message, edit or retry sent the moment a reply ends waits for the branch to be free instead of being refused as still running. A new chat shows its first message at once.
- **Replies read as text.** Passages of one reply that a tool call, a steer or shown reasoning came between are separated by a blank line in `--print`, channels, search, titles, copy, the OpenAI-compatible route, the terminal and ACP. A reply that paused for an answer and went on keeps the text from before the pause.
- **Windows.** The App window leaves the wait page: the Worker is recognised by its real command line, each account's Worker settles its own port, and a port held by another program is named with how to change it. A failed first run can be retried, installs work where scripts are restricted, and a terminal install works under a user folder with Chinese, accented letters or spaces.
- **macOS and Linux installs.** Packages are chosen for the interpreter's own architecture, Intel Macs and macOS 13 get matching packages, and a Linux terminal install without browser libraries finishes.
- **Sign-in.** A ChatGPT sign-in shared by two installs on one machine is renewed by both, and each adopts the other's newer login instead of failing with an expired token.
- **Projects.** A project created, renamed or removed anywhere appears in every open page and open project menu, and a project re-created at a removed folder takes the new name.
- A deleted or unknown conversation answers "not found" instead of an invented context estimate.

## 🚀 Improvements

- **Long conversations open quickly.** A long conversation opens in a fraction of a second after a restart instead of 8–13 s, start-up no longer reads every conversation, and opening one no longer holds Send or Stop behind it.
- **Smaller conversation logs.** Besides the reply itself, a turn adds about an eighth of what it used to add to the conversation's log, and a very long reply is read in linear time. A reply cut off mid-stream keeps each finished passage, so search still finds it.
- **A responsive server.** The project list answers in milliseconds however many projects there are, and a slow folder read, a file lookup or a wait for a busy conversation no longer holds a Send or Stop behind it.
- **Provider logos.** Popular providers' logos sit on each vendor's own light or dark plate with the same margin, and provider rows keep to the pane.
- **A new Goal is one bubble.** It starts with a coloured Goal label on the goal's own first line, instead of a "Goal saved" line plus a bubble.
- **File links stand apart.** File links in replies carry a faint underline, so they are not mistaken for plain code.
- **Install and Download pages follow the newest release.** Every App link on them resolves to the newest version's file, so they never point at an old one.
- **Leaner releases.** A release uploads each installer once, under its versioned name; `release-manifest.json` lists the SHA-256 of every file.
- A deleted conversation leaves only its marker behind, and its file history goes when no other conversation uses that folder's history.

On macOS, open the DMG and copy `OpenProgram.app` to `/Applications`. On Windows, run the installer; it installs for your user only. The release manifest lists the SHA-256 of every file. A file whose name ends in `-unsigned` was built without a publisher signature; see "Unsigned packages" below when that applies.

### CLI / Server

Install this release on macOS or Linux; the installer selects the architecture and verifies the runtime:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://fuzzykuji.github.io/openprogram-site/install | OPENPROGRAM_VERSION=1.3.0 sh
```

On Windows x64, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://fuzzykuji.github.io/openprogram-site/install.ps1 | iex
```

## 🔄 Upgrade guide

- **Desktop on macOS:** use **Check for updates** in Settings, or download the matching DMG above and replace the application in `/Applications`.
- **Desktop on Linux:** use **Check for updates** in Settings; the new version installs in place.
- **Desktop on Windows:** use **Check for updates** in Settings, or run the installer above; it installs over the existing App and keeps your data.
- **CLI / Server:** run `openprogram upgrade`, or repeat the versioned installation command above.
- **Your data:** configuration, conversations, Programs, and saved progress under `~/.openprogram` are preserved.
- **After upgrading:** check `openprogram --version`.

See the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/FuzzyKuji/OpenProgram/blob/v1.3.0/docs/install/upgrade.html) for details.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/FuzzyKuji/OpenProgram/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0)
